overview: This Senate resolution supports naming May 2026 "Renewable Fuels Month." Renewable fuels include ethanol (usually made from corn), biodiesel and renewable diesel (made from sources like soybean oil, used cooking oil, and animal fats), and sustainable aviation fuel. The resolution credits these fuels with lowering prices at the pump, cutting greenhouse gas emissions compared with petroleum fuels, supporting farmers and rural jobs, and reducing reliance on foreign oil. It also mentions the federal Renewable Fuel Standard, which requires a certain amount of renewable fuel to be blended into the nation's fuel supply. The resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or spending. The Senate approved it by voice vote on May 21, 2026.
for: Supporters say renewable fuels support farm and rural economies, add to the domestic fuel supply, and reduce emissions, and deserve recognition.
against: Critics say the resolution presents only the benefits of renewable fuels, whose environmental and price effects are debated, and it is symbolic, changing no law.
